overall: The AG found no Open Meeting Law violation: the council president, as chair, could cut off a public speaker's remarks during public comment, and the AG declined the separate free speech claim as outside its jurisdiction.

allegations.summary: A member of the public alleges the council president cut off his remarks at the June 12, 2012 meeting and prevented him from finishing while he addressed the council.
allegations.key_passage: Because the Council President, as the chair of the Council, has the authority to decide who may address the Council, he did not violate the Open Meeting Law by cutting off Mr. Cardimino's remarks.

allegations.summary: The complainant also alleged that the council president violated his constitutional right to free speech by cutting off his remarks.
allegations.key_passage: The Division of Open Government only interprets and enforces the Open Meeting Law, thus we decline to review allegations of violation of any other laws.
